stage1_error: Stage 1 applied Arizona's 200% gross limit to all 12 months of 2026 and got 12 × $24 = $288. It said it could not confirm when the 200% standard took effect. Arizona used a 185% ECE standard before 200%: the CNAP manual has an archived '185% of Federal Poverty Level (Expanded Categorical Eligibility)' page, and DB101 Arizona gives 185% ($2,414 for one person) for October 1, 2025 – September 30, 2026. The household's gross income (about $2,539) is above that 185% limit. So in the months before the 200% standard (January–February 2026, per the engine's March start) the household is not categorically eligible, and the $58,700 bank balance fails the $4,500 elderly/disabled resource limit. Those months pay $0, which gives $240, not $288. Stage 1's other steps are correct: categorical eligibility waives the asset and net-income tests, the formula benefit is $0, the $24 minimum applies to eligible one-person households, and FY2026 parameters run through December under the freeze.
summary: The household is one person, 80 and disabled, with about $2,539–$2,545 a month in gross income. That is above 185% of the poverty guideline ($2,413/mo) but below 200% ($2,608/mo). When Arizona's expanded categorical eligibility (ECE) limit is 200%, the household is categorically eligible, so there is no asset or net-income test. As an eligible one-person household it gets the $24 FY2026 minimum, even though its formula benefit is $0. Arizona's manual moved from a 185% ECE standard (now archived) to 200% during FY2026, after a 185% table that ran from October 2025. For the months still under 185%, the household fails the $4,500 elderly/disabled resource test and the net-income test, so it gets $0. Ten months × $24 = $240, which is the engine's own result and stands.
